items.title: Preserve current memory lineage in cognitive context
items.problem: The cognitive request contains memory IDs, sources and confidence but drops version, evidence and update time. Corrected memories therefore lose inspectable lineage before inference.
items.expectedBehavior: Serialize current same-conversation memory descriptors with their exact version, evidence references and updatedAt alongside existing grounded fields. Preserve request data, scope isolation and existing context bounds.
acceptanceCriteria: Every included memory has the exact supplied current version, ordered evidence references and updatedAt; no invented or altered lineage fields.
Fresh corrected-memory and empty-evidence fixtures retain their actual descriptors without elevating confidence.
Mixed-scope and foreign-only inputs never expose foreign IDs, content or evidence anywhere in the completion request.
Normal request, bounded context and protected scope checks remain green.
nonGoals: Changing persistent memory schema, consolidation, retention or author eligibility.
Claiming improved model recall or judgment solely from request serialization.
materialRisks: Evidence references can consume context capacity or contain instruction-like text; they remain untrusted prompt data.
Source-version metadata is useful evidence, not automatic trust or permission.

items.title: Bound memory context in UTF-8 bytes while retaining newest experiences
items.problem: Twelve four-thousand-character memories do not establish a total byte bound. Unicode content and evidence references can exceed intended memory-context resources.
items.expectedBehavior: Select same-conversation memories newest first, using updatedAt with deterministic original-position tie breaking. Emit at most twelve descriptors, each content a nonempty source prefix of at most four thousand characters, with the JSON-serialized memory array at most 32768 UTF-8 bytes. Preserve exact lineage for each retained descriptor.
acceptanceCriteria: The UTF-8 byte length of JSON.stringify(prompt.memories) is at most 32768 for fresh mixed ASCII, multibyte Unicode and large-evidence inputs.

Choose eligible experiences in descending updatedAt order, resolving equal times by later input position first, and retain the newest whenever its complete descriptor can fit with a nonempty grounded content prefix.
Emit at most twelve descriptors; content remains a nonempty source prefix of at most four thousand characters and never ends with a newly isolated surrogate from truncation.
If immutable metadata cannot fit even with a minimal grounded content prefix, omit that descriptor rather than changing its evidence, version, source, confidence or update time.
Preserve P06-memory-provenance behavior, ordinary experience retention when it fits, request data and foreign-scope exclusion.
nonGoals: Bounding the user's request bytes or total provider prompt independently of memory context.
Dropping or rewriting evidence to make a descriptor fit.
Changing storage order, persistence or fairness among the standing growth dimensions.
materialRisks: A smaller context can omit useful older episodes; newest-first selection and exact omitted-state accounting must be stated honestly.
Byte accounting must include JSON escaping, metadata and array delimiters, not only content characters.
An oversized latest descriptor can be omitted; preserving exact provenance takes precedence over including it.
